title: Kedgeree
subtitle: Anglo-Indian smoked haddock and rice breakfast dish
excerpt: Smoked haddock flaked through lightly spiced basmati rice with hard-boiled eggs and fresh parsley. A Victorian Anglo-Indian breakfast dish that works equally well for lunch or a light supper.

recipe.sourceNotes: Kedgeree is an Anglo-Indian hybrid that developed in the British colonial period in India. It is derived from the Indian dish khichdi, a simple, nourishing mixture of rice and lentils or split peas that was eaten by Indian workers. British colonists adopted and transformed it, substituting smoked fish and hard-boiled eggs for the lentils and adding curry spice. It was brought back to Britain and became fashionable in Victorian households as a breakfast dish from the chafing dish at the sideboard. It remains popular as a brunch and light supper dish. The version here uses smoked haddock, the most common British version, though other smoked fish work equally well. The recipe pairs with the kedgeree-smoked-salmon variation.

recipeTools.notes: Two saucepans: one for rice, one for poaching the fish.

content.text: Poach the haddock in milk rather than water: it produces a more delicate, creamy flavour and the poaching milk can be reserved and used in the dish. Do not overcook the fish or it will become dry and fibrous: 8 minutes at a gentle simmer is enough for a thick piece. The rice should be cooked until just tender so the grains stay separate when combined with the fish.
Poach the smoked haddock in the milk with the bay leaves for 8 minutes at a gentle simmer. Remove the fish and set aside. Strain and reserve 150 ml of the poaching milk, discarding the rest.
Cook the rice in a saucepan of salted water according to the packet instructions, or until just tender. Drain and set aside.
Melt the butter in a wide pan over medium heat. Fry the onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add the curry powder and turmeric. Cook for 1 minute.

Flake the fish, discarding skin and bones. Add the rice to the pan and stir gently to combine with the spiced onion. Pour in the reserved poaching milk. Fold in the flaked fish. Squeeze over the lemon juice. Heat through gently for 2 minutes. Season with salt. Scatter with parsley and arrange the egg quarters on top.
